items.title: Pay 'Aktualisierungsgebühr' (fee demand)
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar date for payment: 'zahlbar bis 30.11.2026'. This is used as written (no period to count, no weekend/holiday adjustment needed since 30 Nov 2026 is a Monday, and in any case this is not a genuine authority demand).

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a scam/phishing fee demand: there is no real German authority named 'Zentralregister Fahrzeugdaten Deutschland' — vehicle registration (Zulassung) and holder data are administered by the local Zulassungsstelle and the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt, not by any private 'central register' that mails fee invoices.

The payment is requested to a foreign (Lithuanian) IBAN made out to a private individual ('R. Kazlauskas'), which is inconsistent with any genuine German public authority or official vehicle register — official German bodies do not collect fees via personal foreign bank accounts.

The letter uses a pressure tactic ('Ohne Aktualisierung kann die Zulassung ab Januar 2027 ruhen' / threat to report the case to the Zulassungsstelle if unpaid) typical of fake official-looking collection letters (comparable to fake 'Gewerbeauskunft'-style registries).

Recommendation: do not pay this invoice; verify any claimed issue with your actual local Zulassungsstelle directly and consider reporting this letter as potential fraud (e.g. to the Verbraucherzentrale or police).
